hooks.text: Astronauts floating in orbit are still trapped by Earth's gravity.
Earth's gravity at the space station is nearly ninety percent strong.
Why do astronauts float if Earth's gravity is still ninety percent strong?

title: Why Astronauts Never Escape Earth's Gravity
description: Think astronauts in orbit are completely weightless? Discover why Earth's gravity is actually nearly 90 percent as strong on the space station.

beats.text: Astronauts floating in orbit are still trapped by Earth's gravity.
beats.visual: photograph of the International Space Station orbiting Earth, NASA, 2021

beats.text: In 1961, Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov reported the first case of space sickness.
beats.visual: official portrait of Soviet Cosmonaut Gherman Titov in flight suit, 1961

beats.text: This sickness occurs even though space is actually not a gravity-free vacuum.
beats.visual: illustration of gravity field lines wrapping around the Earth

beats.text: At the altitude of the space station, Earth's gravity is nearly ninety percent as strong as on the ground.
beats.visual: diagram comparing Earth gravity strength at sea level and orbital altitude

beats.text: Normal gravity on Earth's surface pulls at approximately nine point eight meters per second squared.
beats.visual: illustration of Earth with gravity equation and gravity potato model

beats.text: In orbit, gravity is still highly active, but spacecraft are in constant free fall.
beats.visual: photograph of NASA astronaut floating inside the International Space Station, 2018

beats.text: High horizontal speed lets them continuously fall over the curving horizon of the Earth.
